acceptance_criteria.criterion: ledger_list_projects returns projects from all configured stores, each tagged with store_id and store_label
ledger_initialize_project creates a new project in the correct store — the first store whose .repositories.json claims the repository
ledger_initialize_project for a repository not registered in any store returns an error containing "not registered in any store"
ledger_detect_project searches all stores when resolving a cwd_path and returns MULTI_STORE_AMBIGUOUS with tagged candidates for cross-store collisions
In single-store mode (no stores.json), all operations behave identically to the current implementation

summary: Modified project-lifecycle.ts to delegate reads to MultiStoreManager and writes to StoreRouter.
detectProject() now calls getMultiStoreManager().detectProjectByCwd() and handles the new MULTI_STORE_AMBIGUOUS branch, returning a formatted error listing store IDs and slugs.

listProjects() calls getMultiStoreManager().listAllProjects() when the store context is initialized, returning TaggedProjectMeta[] entries with store_id and store_label for all configured stores. Falls back to LedgerStore.listAllProjects(_ledgerRoot) when context is uninitialized (test override path).

initializeProject() guards multi-store routing with isStoreContextInitialized() && getStoreRouter().isMultiStoreMode(). When active, derives repoName via deriveRepoName(), calls resolveStoreForWrite(), and returns 'not registered in any store' on failure. Single-store path uses LedgerStore(args.project_path) unchanged.

getProjectStatus() bypasses resolveProjectPath() for cwd_path resolution when the store context is initialized — calls getMultiStoreManager().detectProjectByCwd() and handles MULTI_STORE_AMBIGUOUS and AMBIGUOUS branches inline. After path resolution, resolveStoreForRepo() determines the correct ledger root in multi-store mode.
Added isStoreContextInitialized() to store-context.ts — guards multi-store code paths in tool handlers to avoid breaking existing tests that do not call setStoreContext().
Added detectProject to _internal export for testability.
Created mcp-server/tests/tools/project-lifecycle-multi-store.test.ts with 13 integration tests covering all 5 acceptance criteria.
Full test suite: 130 files, 3777 tests — all pass (13 new tests added).

comments.note: project-resolver.ts still calls LedgerStore.detectProjectByCwd() directly. Tools other than project-lifecycle.ts (work-package tools, pipeline tools etc.) use resolveProjectPath() which does single-store detection. Updating project-resolver.ts to use the store context would extend multi-store cwd detection to all tools — out of scope for WP-007 but worth tracking as a follow-up.

getProjectStatus() now has two code paths for cwd resolution (multi-store bypass and legacy resolveProjectPath). If project-resolver.ts is eventually updated to use MultiStoreManager, the bypass can be removed, simplifying getProjectStatus() back to a single resolution call.

The _internal export in project-lifecycle.ts now includes detectProject alongside the other functions. This enables direct unit testing of detectProject without routing through the MCP server registration — a pattern worth applying to other tool functions that currently have no direct test exposure.

summary: Build check: TypeScript compilation clean — no errors.
Targeted test run: all 13 new multi-store integration tests pass (project-lifecycle-multi-store.test.ts).
Full regression: 3787 tests across 131 files — all pass. No regressions introduced.
AC1 verified: listProjects in multi-store mode returns projects from all stores tagged with store_id and store_label; status filter and ARCHIVED exclusion both work cross-store.
AC2 verified: initializeProject routes to the store whose .repositories.json claims the repo — two routing tests (personal and work store) confirm correct store selection.
AC3 verified: unregistered repo returns isError=true with message containing 'not registered in any store' and the repo name.
AC4 verified: detectProject triggers MULTI_STORE_AMBIGUOUS when cwd_path matches projects in two stores; error lists both store_ids; FOUND returned for single-match; NOT_FOUND for no-match.
AC5 verified: single-store (legacy) mode passes 2 explicit tests and the full pre-existing 3764-test suite — all operations behave identically to pre-WP-007 behavior.
isStoreContextInitialized() guard correctly prevents multi-store code paths from activating in existing test suites that don't call setStoreContext().
Vitest default isolation (per-file worker processes) prevents singleton state leakage between the new multi-store test file and existing test files.

metrics.test_coverage: 13 new tests covering all 5 ACs; 3774 pre-existing regression tests pass

comments.note: initializeProject's catch block around resolveStoreForWrite() is a bare catch {} — any file-system error (e.g. corrupted registry file) would surface as the 'not registered in any store' message rather than the actual I/O error. Consider re-throwing non-'not found' errors to preserve diagnostic fidelity. Not a blocking issue since resolveStoreForWrite() primarily throws on lookup failure.

No explicit test for listProjects in multi-store mode with zero projects in all stores. The function correctly returns [] (verified by code inspection — JSON.stringify([]) is valid and the function's catch path would surface any error). A future test addition would harden this edge case.
No improvement — code is clean and consistent with WP-007 deliverables. All 5 ACs are fully met.

summary: WP-007 code-review PASS with one Fix-Forward applied.
store-context.ts: Clean singleton module. isStoreContextInitialized() guard is a well-reasoned compatibility shim — parallels the existing client-info.ts pattern. Documentation is thorough.

project-lifecycle.ts (detectProject): Correct full delegation to getMultiStoreManager().detectProjectByCwd(). All four result states (FOUND, MULTI_STORE_AMBIGUOUS, AMBIGUOUS, NOT_FOUND) handled with clear error messages.

project-lifecycle.ts (listProjects): In-memory filtering approach is consistent with the existing single-store path. Passing no status to listAllProjects() and filtering post-load is deliberate and correct.

project-lifecycle.ts (initializeProject): Multi-store routing is clean and well-guarded. Fix-Forward applied: narrowed the bare catch {} around resolveStoreForWrite() to distinguish unexpected I/O errors from expected 'not registered in any store' errors. Both paths still return isError:true — no behavioral change, QA validation remains intact.

project-lifecycle.ts (getProjectStatus): The cwd_path multi-store bypass is correctly conditioned on !args.project_path && isStoreContextInitialized(). The dual resolution paths are a known trade-off documented by the Developer.

Test file (project-lifecycle-multi-store.test.ts): Comprehensive. All 5 ACs are covered with 13 tests. restoreLegacyContext() in afterEach is a solid pattern for singleton isolation. process.argv manipulation in AC5 is pragmatic and uses try/finally correctly.

comments.note: Narrowed bare catch {} around getStoreRouter().resolveStoreForWrite() in initializeProject() to distinguish 'not registered in any store' errors (expected) from unexpected I/O / schema errors. I/O errors now surface the actual message via a dedicated return branch instead of the misleading 'not registered' instruction. Both paths return isError:true — no behavioral change; QA validation remains intact.

detectProject() and getProjectStatus() each contain near-identical MULTI_STORE_AMBIGUOUS candidate formatting blocks (candidates.map(c => `[store_id: ${c.store_id}] ${c.slug}`).join(', ')). If a third tool adds the same cwd-detection bypass this pattern will triplicate. A private formatMultiStoreAmbiguous() helper would DRY this up — low urgency while only two call sites exist.

[documentation-forward] project-resolver.ts still calls LedgerStore.detectProjectByCwd() directly (single-store only). Tools that rely on resolveProjectPath() (work-package, pipeline tools) will not benefit from multi-store cwd detection until project-resolver.ts is updated. This gap is noted by the Developer but should be surfaced in the API surface docs so future contributors know which tools have full multi-store support and which do not.
